question: My work permit expired before I applied for an extension. Can I keep working while I apply to restore my status?
generated_answer:
Yes, you can continue working while your application to restore your status is being processed. However, you must apply to restore your status within 90 days of your work permit expiring. If your application is approved, you will be able to continue working until a decision is made on your new work permit application. If your application is refused, you will not be able to continue working and will need to leave Canada.

To apply to restore your status, you will need to submit an application to the IRCC and pay the required fees. You will also need to provide evidence that you meet the requirements for the work permit, such as a job offer and proof of qualifications.

It's important to note that restoring your status does not automatically grant you a new work permit. You will need to apply for a new work permit after your status has been restored. If you are unable to obtain a new work permit, you will need to leave Canada.

To avoid any issues, it's recommended that you apply to restore your status as soon as possible after your work permit expires. This will give you the best chance of being able to continue working while your application is being processed.

Here are the steps to apply to restore your status:

1. Gather all required documents, including proof of your previous work permit, job offer, and proof of qualifications.
2. Complete the application form to restore your status, which can be found on the IRCC website.
3. Pay the required fees, which are currently $200 for restoring your status and $155 for a new work permit.
4. Submit your application to the IRCC, either online or by mail.
5. Wait for a decision on your application to restore your status. If approved, you can continue working while your new work permit application is being processed.

Remember to keep track of the 90-day deadline and apply to restore your status as soon as possible after your work permit expires. This will help minimize any disruption to your work and ensure that you can continue working while your application is being processed.
